messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: new web site
parts:
I redesigned the web site for Stan over the weekend.

You can find it at:

https://github.com/stan-dev/webpages

The actual site is all linked from:

mc-stan.org/index.html

Of course, we have the ultimate "bike shed issue" now:

What color should the web site be?

I'm sort of partial to the pistachio I went with, but
am not wedded to it.

Any other style and content suggestions welcome.

One issue I have given that we list the development team
is where we should draw the line in terms of contribution.
I added Allen Riddell, who's making ongoing contributions
for PyStan. Should I add a section for people who've done
significant work on one piece of Stan, like Rob Goedman's
refactoring of the parser? I'm trying to take care of at
least thanking everyone in the manual.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new web site
parts:
What you're suggesting is definitely more standard
and I would have done it that way if I could figure out
the CSS for it.  The floated navbar doesn't want to run
top to bottom.

One alternative would be to make the text fixed width,
which is also popular.  But I really hate that as a web
site user.  For instance, GitHub's layout's a pain --- it
wants to suck up half my screen.

For a text-heavy site like this I prefer fixed-width for readability,
but I'm not wedded to it (with a reasonable width, of course).

Alternatively I think you can just throw a dummy div behind the
navbar that extends down to the footer and that should prevent
the wrapping, no?

I was trying to avoid blue because it's so common.

I'd love to go with an orange, but couldn't figure out
how to do that in a way that wasn't too neon or too faded.

Black-orange-white -- good colors! http://www-prod-storage.cloud.caltech.edu.s3.amazonaws.com/caltech_designer_specifications.pdf

I can't say I'm a huge fan of orange (doesn't seem very Stan-ny to me)
but the way to do it would be to use it as an accent and not the
header/footer background.

So, for example, have the navbar black with white white text turn
into orange with black text on rollover and separate the header/footer
with an orange line instead of explicit background.  Or perhaps even
black header/footer with an orange line highlighting the border
(think enough that it doesn't look like a shadow).

I didn't even know it was MIT-ish.  But it's a bit too corporate
for me.

I've been using a deep purple color scheme (with bright green for accents,
although I wouldn't use the green for a site like this) for my slides to which
I've grown accustomed.  

Maybe something like 6 or 10 here http://blog.crazyegg.com/2012/07/11/website-color-palettes/?

You thought green with yellow popups was garish and you're going with
purple and bright green!

Didn't like those, but liked 2 and 5 and sort of liked 1 until

bakery". We're more of an Easy-Bake Oven :-)

I went with a medium and muted version of pistachio. We can
choose a different color, but I don't want to get into a more
complicated design unless someone else wants to take over the CSS
duties.

- Bob
